full_text.source: Scientific Reports full text supplied in prompt

eligibility.evidence: Overview of study, pp. 2–3: compares ChatGPT story-retelling performance with human retellings in a serial-reproduction task, using the same stories and instructions.

A.title: Humans create more novelty than ChatGPT when asked to retell a story

models.name: ChatGPT
models.version: ChatGPT3 (stable version; exact model checkpoint not reported)

paradigms.name: Serial reproduction of narratives (story retelling in three successive iterations)
paradigms.source_paper: Breithaupt, Li, and Kruschke (2022), “Serial reproduction of narratives preserves emotional appraisals”
paradigms.location: Overview of study, pp. 2–3; Results, pp. 3–7

D.population: Amazon Mechanical Turk participants who retold stories; 531 Prolific participants rated ChatGPT retellings. Prior published human retelling data were also used.
D.metric: Word and synset transmission/change; grammatical-category proportions; age of acquisition; human ratings of happiness, sadness, imagery, and emotional impact.

effects.label: ATTENUATED
effects.location: Results, pp. 3–7; Figs. 1–4. Human retellings created approximately 55–60% novel synsets per iteration; ChatGPT showed fewer novel synsets and less change across retellings. Statistical details and data: OSF project jr2py.

E.headline: ChatGPT quickly condenses stories and changes little afterward, while humans continually invent concepts; both preserve the stories’ emotional appraisals.

G.notes: The exact ChatGPT checkpoint, query dates, and decoding settings are not reported. The paper describes human retelling data from a prior study as well as a Prolific rating sample; clarify the participant counts and role of each dataset when interpreting the human comparison.
